paragraphs.text: Fish cannot be seen from a satellite, but the boats that catch them can. Since 2016 researchers have used the radio signals that vessels send to build a map of fishing activity across the world’s oceans.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The maps produced a surprise. More than half of the ocean surface is fished, and the busiest areas are not near the coasts of poor countries but in international waters, where a small number of fleets work far from home.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Governments have begun to use the data. One island state used it to show that vessels were fishing inside its protected zone, and a court accepted the maps as evidence for the first time in 2019.
paragraphs.label: C
